archive_alive:
''[[w:Wayback Machine|Wayback Machine]]'' is the name of a website used to archive the contents of other websites, as they were retrieved at different dates when they were alive.

There is usually no need to translate it, except maybe in languages that use common transliterations (sometimes standardized) for terms not written in their native script, including for proper names or brands.

Be aware that translating or transliterating names of external web sites may cause confusion (unless these alternate names are endorsed and used by these sites for the translation they propose or in their documentation and official communications. For brands, company names, and even people proper names, their actual translation supported may not be literal, with completely different terms adapted for other local markets they are targeting, or because of local agreements with other local organizations, or because of local law.

You may need emphasize the foreign term, or its translation or transliteration, using “quotation marks” or ''italics'', to avoid confusion with generic terms.

maineditsummaryplaceholder:
Hint identifying the configurable summary for the main article edit. This help text is not the summary itself. The field accepts bot counter placeholders and optional conditional clauses; see the syntax notes below.

This is configuration help for translators, not a request to change the wiki's current summary. Administrators opt into detailed summaries in this field; existing configured summaries continue to work. These five optional counters describe main-article changes, not talk-only suggestions or Wikidata's separate edit logic:
* <nowiki>{deadlinksrescued}</nowiki>: first archive added for a source classified as dead.
* <nowiki>{livelinksarchived}</nowiki>: first archive added for a source not classified as dead. This does not guarantee that the source was independently confirmed alive.
* <nowiki>{archivesreplaced}</nowiki>: existing archive links replaced.
* <nowiki>{archivesrepaired}</nowiki>: existing archives whose markup/usage was repaired or normalized.
* <nowiki>{deadtagsremoved}</nowiki>: obsolete dead-link tags removed.

Legacy counters include <nowiki>{linksrescued}</nowiki> (the broader rescue total), <nowiki>{linkstagged}</nowiki> (unfixable dead sources newly marked dead), <nowiki>{linksmodified}</nowiki> (rescued plus tagged), <nowiki>{linksanalyzed}</nowiki> (links examined), and <nowiki>{linksarchived}</nowiki> (successful submissions to the Wayback Machine, not archive-link insertions).

An optional clause has the form <nowiki>{ifany:countername:text}</nowiki>. Its text is included only when the named counter is greater than zero; otherwise the entire clause is omitted. For example, <nowiki>{ifany:deadlinksrescued:Rescued {deadlinksrescued} dead sources.}</nowiki>. Translate the readable clause text, but keep ifany, counter names, braces, and separator colons unchanged. Put punctuation/separating spaces inside a clause when they should disappear with it. Single-brace configuration tokens are different from the interface's double-brace substitutions.

Displayed numbers may use localized digits; conditional clauses still test the underlying numeric counts. The syntax does not choose grammatical singular/plural forms automatically, and MediaWiki PLURAL/GENDER constructs are not evaluated by this interface. Use wording that works with the counts. Only translate the help itself here; translating this message does not alter any saved wiki configuration. An opted-in conditional summary that evaluates to blank uses the existing rescue/tagging fallback rather than saving an empty explanation.
errortalkeditsummary: Configuration-field label for the wiki edit summary attached when posting an archive-failure notice on a talk page. It is not the body of the error message.
errortalkeditsummaryplaceholder: Hint describing the edit summary for a talk-page archive-error notice. The summary appears in revision history; the notice body is configured separately. Detailed main-article action counters are not supplied for this summary.
talkeditsummary: Configuration-field label for the wiki edit summary attached when posting an ordinary talk-page notification.
talkeditsummaryplaceholder: Hint describing the revision-history summary for talk-page messages, distinct from the talk-message body and main article-edit summary. Detailed main-article action counters are not supplied here.
definearchivetemplateshead: Heading of the administrator tool defining how archive templates are recognized and generated.
archivetemplateslistheader: Section heading listing all configured archive-template rules. A rule may describe more than one archive service's syntax.
templatename: Field label for an archive rule's internal name. Despite the label, this field is not necessarily the literal on-wiki template name.
templatenameplaceholder: Hint clarifying that this value names the archive rule inside IABot, rather than naming a template page on Wikipedia.
archivetemplatedefinitions: Field label for the parameter/syntax pattern defining an archive template's behavior.
archivetemplatedefinitionsplaceholder: Hint with an executable archive-rule example. Keep parameter spellings, placeholders such as {url}, {date14}, {archiveurl}, service selectors {@wayback...}/{@default...}, braces, pipes, and equals signs intact. Translate the surrounding explanation; these are syntax examples, not natural-language sentences.
templatebehavior: Configuration label choosing whether an archive/dead-link template is appended to the source link or replaces/wraps its markup.
template-append: Template-behavior option that places the generated template after the original URL/link instead of replacing it.
template-swallow: Template-behavior option that replaces the original URL/link markup with a template that carries it. “Swallow” in the key is an internal term for wrapping/replacement.
createarchivetemplate: Heading/action label for creating an archive-template rule in IABot. This does not create a template page on the wiki.
editarchivetemplate:
Heading for editing the named archive-template rule. template is the configured rule name.

Parameters are inserted by IABot, not MediaWiki template calls. Keep each complete token unchanged, including its English name and double braces; it may be repositioned where grammar allows:
* <nowiki>{{template}}</nowiki>: the archive-rule name being edited.
archivetemplatesyntaxerror: Validation error when an archive-template rule's parameter/mapping syntax cannot be parsed.
archivedefinesuccess: Confirmation that a new archive-template rule was saved successfully.
deprecated: Annotation for an archive-template option that is discouraged/obsolete. “Deprecated” is the software term, not necessarily completely unsupported.
chooseconfigurepage: Prompt to choose one of the available system-configuration sections.
deadlink_tags_data: Configuration-field label for the parameter pattern used to recognize/generate a dead-link template, distinct from the list of template names.
deadlink_tags_dataplaceholder: Hint with a dead-link-template parameter pattern. Keep {url}, permadead, braces, colons, pipes, and the literal example parameter names/values unchanged; {permadead:yes:no} chooses yes for a permanently dead URL and no otherwise.
deadlink_tags_dataclear: Help explaining that clearing the field removes the saved dead-link-template syntax. “Delete this” means empty the field's contents, not delete a wiki template page.
dateformat: Configuration-field label for the date formats recognized/used on this wiki when processing citation dates.
dateformatplaceholder:
Hint explaining that date patterns use strftime-style tokens, such as %Y, %m, and %d. These tokens are executable formatting syntax and must not be translated.

If referring to extended rule syntax, keep <nowiki>@default:</nowiki> and <nowiki> on match </nowiki> unchanged as parser keywords; regular expressions and percent-format tokens must remain valid.
tag_cites: Setting label choosing how dead status is recorded for sources already inside citation templates.
tag_cites0: Citation-tagging option appending a separate dead-link template to the citation.
tag_cites1: Citation-tagging option recording dead status in the citation template's own mapped dead-link parameter rather than appending a separate tag.
runpages: Title of the interface page for viewing and changing the bot's per-wiki runpage enable/disable status.
enabled: Bot run-status value meaning enabled for regular operation on the selected wiki. Appears after the runpage-status label.
gotorunpage: Link/button opening the selected wiki's on-wiki bot runpage, where its operating status is controlled.
runpagedisabled: Status indicating that runpage control is not enabled/configured for this wiki. This is different from a configured runpage whose bot status is currently off.
enable: Runpage control button to enable the bot on the selected wiki. Use an action verb, as opposed to the status value Enabled.
disable: Runpage control button to disable the bot on the selected wiki. Use an action verb, as opposed to the status value Disabled.
togglerunpagesuccess: Confirmation that the requested change to the bot's runpage operating status succeeded.
runpageenable: Log action recording that the bot was enabled through runpage control. The acting user and wiki are supplied by the log layout.
runpagedisable: Log action recording that the bot was disabled through runpage control.
runpageerror: Heading for a failure while inspecting or changing the bot's runpage state.
norunpageerror: Error explaining that ordinary runpage control is unavailable for this wiki and only the installation's root administrator can change the bot's operating state.
togglerunpage: Permission description allowing a user to enable or disable the bot on the wikis where they hold that interface permission.
citerules: Title of the tool for configuring citation-template recognition, parameter maps, and defaults.
citetemplates: Configuration-section label for the global list of citation-template names across supported wikis.
citerulescatheader: Heading grouping the citation-configuration sections: template list, parameter mappings, and defaults.
cite_listplaceholder: Hint for editing the global citation-template list. Enter literal transclusions such as <nowiki>{{cite web}}</nowiki>, one per line, using actual wiki-template names. Preserve braces; this list is executable configuration, not a prose inventory.
importcitoid: Button importing or refreshing citation metadata from the selected wiki, including available template data. Citoid is a service/configuration name in the key, not a word that must be added to the displayed label.
citemap: Configuration-section label for mappings between a citation template's actual parameter names and IABot's semantic fields, such as original URL or archive date.
citetemplatedefinitionsplaceholder:
Hint with a citation-parameter mapping example. Preserve literal placeholder names, including {url}, {archiveurl}, {title}, {accesstimestamp:automatic}, {archivetimestamp:automatic}, and deadvalues. The template's real parameter names go on the left of equals signs; values on the right use IABot's mapping syntax. Translate the explanation rather than rewriting the executable example.

The special deadvalues expression supplies the citation template’s actual values for dead, live, usurped, and default states. Its selector name and separators are syntax, not translatable prose.
defaultCite: Configuration-field label for the wiki citation template used by default when converting an eligible plain source into a citation.
defaultCiteplaceholder: Hint asking for the actual on-wiki name of the default citation template. This is configuration data, not a translated descriptive label.
defaultMap: Configuration-field label for the fallback citation-parameter mapping used for this wiki's templates where applicable.
defaultArchiveTitle: Configuration-field label for fallback text used when the bot cannot determine an archive/source title. The field contains title text, not the name of a template parameter.
defaultArchiveTitleplaceholder: Hint explaining that the entered text is used as a fallback archive title when no title can be determined. This is an ordinary text fallback rather than a URL.
citedefaults: Citation-configuration section heading for the default template, parameter map, and fallback archive title.
analysepageerrorheader: Heading for a failure while analyzing a submitted wiki page.
articletoolargeerror:
Error when a wiki article exceeds the single-page tool's processing limit. The link directs the user to submit a queued job instead of partially analyzing the page.

Contains HTML. Translate visible prose and link labels while preserving the markup, link destinations, and substitutions. Do not replace HTML formatting with wiki markup.
debugwarningheader: Warning heading indicating that diagnostic/debug mode is active in this user's session.
debugwarningmessage: Warning that diagnostic mode may expose additional error output and make the tool slower. Signing out and in again ends that session mode.
invokebot: Permission description allowing a user to request an edit from the bot account. This concerns which account saves a wiki edit, not merely viewing an analysis.
incompletetranslationheader: A header indicating that the interface translation is incomplete. Appears before {{msg-wm|Iabot-incompletetranslationmessage}}
incompletetranslationmessage: Message explaining that some messages on the page are not translated yet. Appears after {{msg-wm|Iabot-incompletetranslationheader}}
botisdisabledheader: header explaining that the bot is disabled
botisdisabledmessage: message explaining the bot is disabled but user submitted bot jobs will still run
enabledby: Identifies the user that enabled the bot on a given wiki. 'Enabled by: Example user'
disabledby: Identifies the user that disabled the bot on a given wiki. 'Disabled by: Example user'
timestamp: This is just a one word noun.
auditentryshort: This is a log entry for the checkIfDead scanner. {{status}} uses either the noun "Alive" or "Dead"
auditlogurldata: Header found in the URL manager
curlcontenttype: Scan-detail label for the Content-Type reported by the external server, such as text/html. “Content type” is an HTTP media type, not the subject matter of the page.
do_not_use_this_talk_page: Warning message posted to the bot's talk pages to direct users to the bot's talk page on Meta-Wiki
non-criticaldbfailure: An error message. A "non-critical DB" is a database that is less important for the functioning of the system.
dbqueryerror:
Database-error message showing a query and its failure details in contexts where this diagnostic is used. sqlquery is SQL text, errno a numeric code, and errormessage the database's error explanation. Do not translate the inserted diagnostics themselves.

Parameters are inserted by IABot, not MediaWiki template calls. Keep each complete token unchanged, including its English name and double braces; it may be repositioned where grammar allows:
* <nowiki>{{sqlquery}}</nowiki>: the SQL query text involved in the error.
* <nowiki>{{errno}}</nowiki>: the numeric database error code.
* <nowiki>{{errormessage}}</nowiki>: the database server’s diagnostic text.

Contains HTML. Translate visible prose and link labels while preserving the markup, link destinations, and substitutions. Do not replace HTML formatting with wiki markup.
archivecopy: Used as default link text for links to archived copies of web pages
